title: Constant-to-completed coefficients on derived-complete categories
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $I=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\subset A$ be an ideal. Let $\underline A$ and $\underline{A/I^n}$ be the constant sheaves of rings [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and let $\widehat A=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}\underline{A/I^n}$, with its canonical map $\underline A\to\widehat A$ and projections [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. Let $D(\mathcal O)$ denote the derived category of sheaves of modules over a ring sheaf $\mathcal O$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. An object $M\in D(\mathcal O)$ is derived $I$-complete if, for every object $U$ of $\mathcal C$ and every local section $f\in(I\mathcal O)(U)$, one has $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal O_U[1/f],M|_U)=0$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]; here $\mathcal O_U$ denotes restriction to the slice site over $U$, and $\mathcal O_U[1/f]$ is the sheafification of the presheaf of localizations, placed in degree zero.

The sheaf $\widehat A$ is flat over $\underline A$ (tensoring with it is exact), and for every $n\geq1$ the projection induces a canonical isomorphism $\widehat A/I^n\widehat A\cong\underline{A/I^n}$. Restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] along $\underline A\to\widehat A$ induces an equivalence
$$D_{\mathrm{comp}}(\widehat A,I\widehat A)\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{\mathrm{comp}}(\underline A,I).$$
For every $M\in D(\widehat A)$, restriction of scalars and finite reduction have the canonical comparison isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Res}(M)\otimes^L_{\underline A}\underline{A/I^n}\cong M\otimes^L_{\widehat A}\underline{A/I^n}$$
in $D(\underline{A/I^n})$, with derived change of rings as in [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. These isomorphisms commute with $\underline{A/I^{n+1}}\to\underline{A/I^n}$.
Let $\mathcal C'$ be a second small site and define $\underline A'$, $\underline{A/I^n}'$ and $\widehat A'$ there by the same construction. Let $u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C')\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a morphism of topoi, meaning an adjoint pair $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ with $u^{-1}$ preserving finite limits. Identify $u^{-1}\underline A=\underline A'$ and $u^{-1}\underline{A/I^n}=\underline{A/I^n}'$ by the canonical constant-sheaf maps. Let $c:u^{-1}\widehat A\to\widehat A'$ be the map induced by the finite projections. Write $Lu^*_{\widehat A}$ for derived module pullback along $c$, and $Lu^*_{\underline A}$ for constant-coefficient derived module pullback, computed on K-flat complexes with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-weil-pbc-diagram-kflat-replacements, lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class]. For every $M\in D(\widehat A)$ there are canonical isomorphisms
$$\operatorname{Res}'(Lu^*_{\widehat A}M)\otimes^L_{\underline A'}\underline{A/I^n}'\cong Lu^*_{\underline A}(\operatorname{Res}M\otimes^L_{\underline A}\underline{A/I^n}).$$
These isomorphisms are in $D(\underline{A/I^n}')$. They are natural in $M$ and $u$ and commute with the finite quotient transitions. The canonical comparison $Lu^*_{\underline A}\operatorname{Res}M\to\operatorname{Res}'(Lu^*_{\widehat A}M)$ is induced on K-flat representatives by the scalar-extension map $u^{-1}M\to u^{-1}M\otimes_{u^{-1}\widehat A}\widehat A'$; its finite reductions are the inverses of the displayed isomorphisms. The quotient maps commute with this comparison.

For a strict inverse sequence of complexes, write $R\lim$ for the total right derived inverse limit: take a K-injective resolution in the category of strict inverse sequences and then its termwise inverse limit; K-injectivity means that maps from acyclic tower complexes are null-homotopic [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. This fixes functorial models of the sequential derived limits [def-weil-derived-limit]. Restriction of scalars identifies the sequential derived limits of the finite-reduction towers above and carries the quotient-tower completion unit to the corresponding constant-coefficient completion unit. More explicitly, for $\mathcal O=\underline A$ or $\widehat A$, put
$$Q_m(\mathcal O)=\bigotimes_{j=1}^r[\mathcal O\xrightarrow{a_j^m}\mathcal O]$$
in degrees $[-r,0]$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], with transition maps multiplication by $a_j$ in degree $-1$ and identity in degree $0$ in each factor. For $N\in D(\mathcal O)$ the canonical map
$$N\longrightarrow R\lim_m(N\otimes^L_{\mathcal O}Q_m(\mathcal O))$$
is the derived-completion unit for the local completeness condition in the first paragraph. For these two coefficient sheaves the Koszul completion and $R\lim_n(N\otimes^L_{\mathcal O}\underline{A/I^n})$ are canonically isomorphic, respecting the units; restriction of scalars identifies these isomorphisms. In particular Koszul-derived completeness and the stated local completeness condition agree.

proof.text: Write $R=\underline A$, $B=\widehat A$, and $S_n=\underline{A/I^n}$. For each $U$, the constant-module section theorem applied over the Noetherian ring $A/I^n$ shows that $S_n(U)$ is flat over $A/I^n$, and applied to the quotient maps over $A$ shows their section maps are surjective. The existing flat inverse-limit theorem therefore shows $B(U)=\lim_n S_n(U)$ is flat as an $A$-module. Regard $B$ as a module presheaf over the constant ring presheaf with value $A$. Its presheaf tensor functor preserves finite limits objectwise; flat sheafification makes $B$ flat over $R$. For fixed $a$, apply the same limit theorem with the finite module $A/I^a$. Its tensor-limit isomorphism and the section tensor theorem identify $B(U)\otimes_A A/I^a$ with $\lim_n\underline{A/(I^n+I^a)}(U)=S_a(U)$, because the tower is constant for $n\geq a$. These identifications are the projection maps and commute with restriction in $U$. Sheafifying gives $B/I^aB=S_a$; also $R/I^aR=S_a$ by the section tensor theorem. This proves flatness and all quotient identifications.

proof.text: The ideal $IR$ is generated by the finite list of global constant sections $a_j$. Step 1 gives a flat ring-sheaf map $R\to B$ and the induced quotient isomorphism $R/IR\to B/IB$. Apply the general flat ringed-ideal equivalence to this map and ideal. Its local derived-completeness condition is exactly the condition in the statement, on both sides. Thus restriction gives the asserted equivalence of the full complete subcategories. K3 implements this step by identifying the extended kernel ideal sectionwise, using Noetherian finite generators to construct its finite-type module presentation, and applying flat_ringed_ideal_complete_equivalence with the original quotient map.

Choose a K-flat $B$-complex $P\to M$ with flat terms by the independent-coefficient K-flat resolution theorem. Its restriction is K-flat over $R$: for an acyclic $R$-complex $E_0$, the ordinary total tensor $E_0\otimes_R P$ rebrackets as $(E_0\otimes_R B)\otimes_B P$; the first factor is acyclic by Step 1 and the total tensor is acyclic by K-flatness of $P$. Its terms are flat over $R$: tensoring an injection of $R$-modules first with the flat $R$-module $B$ and then with the flat $B$-module $P^q$ preserves the injection. Consequently both derived reductions are represented by $P\otimes_R S_n$ and $P\otimes_B S_n$. Since $S_n=R/I^nR=B/I^nB$, the first complex is the cokernel of the multiplication map from the finite sum of copies of $P$ indexed by degree-$n$ monomials in the generators $a_j$ to $P$. The second complex is the cokernel of exactly the same map of underlying sheaves; thus both are canonically $P/I^nP$. The comparison sends $p\otimes\bar a$ to $p\otimes\bar a$; its inverse is well-defined because both tensors identify with that quotient. It is $S_n$-linear. Applying $S_{n+1}\to S_n$ on the second tensor factor on either side gives the same map; thus this is a strict-tower identification, natural in $P$, and hence in $M$. Derived change of rings identifies these representatives independently of the replacement. The ordinary reduction unit is the extension/restriction adjunction unit, whose sheafified section formula is 1 tensor m. The prescribed transition formula at scalar 1 makes these units a strict tower map; sectionwise extensionality proves uniqueness. Complex comparison uses the canonical composition isomorphisms for termwise application of functors, retaining the same strict comparison. The ordinary scalar-extension identity, composition and addition laws are checked on the sectionwise extension functor and then preserved by module sheafification; they do not need derived change of rings. Construct the scalar unit from the sectionwise module adjunction units followed by the module sheafification unit. Their naturality gives a natural transformation, with the prescribed sheafified pure-tensor section formula. The coordinate universal property for the ordinary complex-limit unit is proved for an abstract tower functor and its natural unit, then specialized to the strict reduction tower. Give the degreewise limit construction one abstract functor name before specializing the coefficient category; the ordinary limit functor is definitionally the original degreewise construction. K3 implements the ordinary finite comparison by identifying the two scalar-extension left adjoints to restriction from S_n. An R-linear map into an S_n-module is B-linear because the kernel of B to S_n is generated by the image of the kernel of R to S_n. The adjunction comparison sends s tensor m to the same tensor. Scalar-transition maps are the tensor-adjunction lifts of the quotient maps; their pure-tensor formula and tensor generation prove the strict tower comparison and its uniqueness. Q1 proves quotientPresentation_exists as follows. For either coefficient ring, take the existing K-flat resolution of every module complex. Scalar extension sends quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes to quasi-isomorphisms: naturality of its existing derived computation comparison expresses the localized tensor map as a composite of isomorphisms, and localization reflects quasi-isomorphisms; exact restriction of scalars preserves them. A strict-tower map is a quasi-isomorphism precisely when every evaluation is, so the reduction tower functor inverts those resolution maps. Apply the resolving-class theorem on the homotopy category and transport its universal counit to complexes using full faithfulness of precomposition by the homotopy quotient. The comparison is invertible on every K-flat complex, without needing the additional flat-term hypothesis. To construct the completion unit, take the ordinary constant-tower/limit adjunction unit degreewise on complexes. Naturality proves its differential and chain-map equations. The constant-tower functor is exact; its invertible derived comparison lets this unit, followed by the chosen right-derived limit comparison, descend by a left-derived lift. Compose with the universal left-derived lift of the strict reduction unit from constant towers to reduction towers. Only the ordinary unit natural transformation is used; no complex adjunction, counit or triangle identities are needed. Naturality of the right-derived limit comparison proves the unit equation. On ordinary complexes, equality after every limit projection identifies the ordinary adjunction-unit composite with ordinaryUnit. This gives exactly all three QuotientPresentationLaws; no new unproved result or arbitrary object choice is introduced. Q1 packages this construction and its unit normalization first over an abstract abelian coefficient category. A private generic ordinary unit is chosen by the fully proved unique projection formula. Abstract limit uniqueness identifies the ordinary adjunction-unit composite with that morphism. Proof irrelevance identifies its specialization with ordinaryUnit; the concrete coefficient theorem assembles the normalized presentation directly, with no change to the public ordinary unit or its definition. H6 implements finiteDerivedComparison and derivedReductionTowerComparison by applying the proved ordinary comparisons to a flat-term K-flat resolving class. Independent-coefficient K-flat resolutions provide the models; flat scalar restriction preserves both K-flatness and termwise flatness. The natural transformations are first extended through the homotopy localization, using its calculus of right fractions and the resolving-class natural-transformation theorem, then descended through the fully faithful localization precomposition functor. Both computation counits are invertible on the resolving class, so the descended comparison is an isomorphism. Cancelling the computation counits gives exactly the stated normalization equations.

proof.text: Set $R'=\underline A'$, $B'=\widehat A'$ and $S_n'=\underline{A/I^n}'$. An inverse image of topoi is exact on abelian sheaves: it preserves finite limits and all colimits as a left adjoint. It preserves constant sheaves, since the constant object is the coproduct of copies of the terminal object and it preserves those coproducts and the terminal object. It commutes with sheaf tensor products, since their balanced generators-and-relations construction uses colimits and finite products, all preserved by inverse image. The ringed pullback K-flat theorem shows that $u^*_{B}P=u^{-1}P\otimes_{u^{-1}B}B'$ is K-flat with flat terms over $B'$, and that $u^{-1}(\operatorname{Res}P)$ is K-flat with flat terms over $R'$ (apply it to the constant coefficient map $u^{-1}R=R'$). Step 1 on $\mathcal C'$ and the argument of Step 3 show restriction of $u^*_{B}P$ is K-flat over $R'$. The left-hand reduction is therefore the ordinary complex $(u^{-1}P\otimes_{u^{-1}B}B')\otimes_{B'}S_n'$, canonically $u^{-1}P\otimes_{u^{-1}B}S_n'$. The right-hand side is represented by $u^{-1}(P\otimes_R S_n)$, canonically $u^{-1}P\otimes_{R'}S_n'$. Apply $u^{-1}$ to the strict identification of Step 3 and use its compatibility with tensor products. This identifies $u^{-1}P\otimes_{u^{-1}B}S_n\prime$ with $u^{-1}P\otimes_{R\prime}S_n\prime$; explicitly both are $u^{-1}P/I^n u^{-1}P$ and the map sends the class of $p$ to itself. This is precisely the stated finite pullback isomorphism. H6 implements finitePull_existsUnique from the ordinary finite pullback isomorphism. Ringed-topos pullback and scalar extension preserve the flat-term K-flat resolving class, so both iterated derived comparisons are invertible on that class. A private abstract square-descent lemma builds the isomorphism, verifies the displayed formula, and proves uniqueness by resolving-class extensionality. Scalar-extension preservation uses the already proved independent-coefficient change-of-rings K-flat theorem directly, without constructing an identity-topos lift.

proof.text: On these representatives the unreduced comparison is $u^{-1}P\to u^{-1}P\otimes_{u^{-1}B}B'$, $p\mapsto p\otimes1$. After finite reduction it sends $p\otimes\bar a$ to $(p\otimes1)\otimes\bar a$, the inverse of Step 4's isomorphism. Quotient transitions send every such tensor to the tensor with the image of $\bar a$, so they commute with both maps. A map of representatives sends $p$ to its image; all these formulas commute with it. For composable inverse images the two maps send $p$ to $(p\otimes1)\otimes1$, which rebrackets to $p\otimes1$ for the composite. Thus the identifications are natural in $M$ and $u$, including composition, and intertwine the quotient maps. The resolving-class construction identifies the chain maps with the asserted derived comparisons. The insertion map is obtained by forgetting the proved scalar-extension unit to underlying sheaves; its section formula is the same sheafified pure tensor formula, and that formula gives uniqueness. The algebraic inverse-image module functor is additive by its generalized-section addition equation and the underlying-sheaf natural isomorphism. Apply the recorded ringed-topoi derived-pullback theorem to this additive functor. Precomposition by the homotopy quotient induces a fully faithful functor on natural transformations, so its homotopy-level right Kan extension remains universal at the complex level. Transport along quotientCompQhIso and mapHomotopyCategoryFactors; their isomorphism components preserve the K-flat computation property. The derived scalar-comparison and finite-pullback computation equations are recorded with abstract ordinary functors, so their complex-composition conversions are checked generically. Unfolding these predicates gives exactly the original normalized representative equations. H6 implements derivedPullComparison_existsUnique by a second abstract square-descent lemma: only the target pullback computation must be invertible, since the ordinary scalar comparison need not be an isomorphism. Conjugate the ordinary comparison by the two exact restriction computations, extend the resulting natural map from flat-term K-flat models, and use resolving-class extensionality for uniqueness. The normalized scalar-insertion formula is retained verbatim.

proof.text: Restriction of scalars $\operatorname{Res}:\operatorname{Mod}(B)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ is exact (kernels and cokernels are unchanged underlying abelian sheaves), preserves all limits, and is right adjoint to extension $B\otimes_R-$ by the balanced tensor universal property. Extension is exact by Step 1. The same adjunction and exactness hold levelwise in strict inverse-sequence categories. The right-adjoint K-injective theorem applied to these tower categories says restriction carries a K-injective $B$-tower resolution to a K-injective $R$-tower resolution. Applying termwise limits then gives the same underlying complex on both sides. Hence $\operatorname{Res}R\lim X_\bullet=R\lim\operatorname{Res}X_\bullet$ canonically for every strict $B$-tower complex. Apply this to the finite reductions of Step 3. Because restriction sends both the constant tower and its quotient maps to exactly the corresponding constant-coefficient tower and maps, the map from the constant tower into its K-injective resolution, followed by limit, gives the same completion unit after restriction. The strict-tower limit theorem supplies the functorial total derived limits here; no exactness of ordinary countable products on the site is needed. K3 implements derivedLimitRestriction using the natural extension-tensor comparison to prove scalar extension exact, reflection of finite limits by restriction, and the levelwise extension/restriction adjunction to preserve K-injectives. The proved generic towerComparison_existsLimitIso supplies the right-derived comparison. Equality with the chosen ordinary limit comparison follows from every limit projection; cancelling resFactors gives the precise displayed normalization on every complex.

proof.text: For each $\mathcal O=R,B$, apply the ringed Koszul reflector theorem to the global sections $a_1,\ldots,a_r$. Its tower and its degree-zero unit are exactly $Q_m(\mathcal O)$ and the map written in the statement. It identifies the local internal-Hom condition with the invertibility of this unit, and proves that the object on its right is the derived-completion reflector. No Noetherian hypothesis on the ring sheaf $B$ is being inferred. For the chosen K-flat $B$-complex $P$, the complexes $\operatorname{Res}(P\otimes_B Q_m(B))$ and $\operatorname{Res}P\otimes_R Q_m(R)$ are termwise the same finite direct sums of $P$ with the same differentials and transition multiplications. Step 6 identifies their derived limits, and the degree-zero unit maps are identical. Thus restriction identifies the Koszul units as well.

The Noetherian Koszul augmentation theorem gives a strict map $Q_m(A)\to A/I^m$ whose cone tower is pro-zero in $D(A)$. Apply the exact constant-sheaf functor (exactness follows from the section theorem) to obtain a cone tower pro-zero in $D(R)$. Tensor with any $N\in D(R)$ using a single K-flat representative. Total tensor commutes with the finite direct sums and differentials defining the mapping cone, and by K-flatness it sends quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms, so it is an exact derived functor and sends the zero cone transitions to zero. We obtain a strict map $N\otimes^L_R Q_m(R)\to N\otimes^L_R S_m$ with pro-zero cone tower. The strict-tower homotopy-limit theorem says its canonical derived-limit map is an isomorphism. Its augmentations send the degree-zero constant $1$ to its quotient class, so this isomorphism takes the Koszul unit to the quotient unit, not merely the two objects to isomorphic objects. For $N=M\in D(B)$ restrict to $R$: Steps 3, 6 and 7 identify the two towers, their maps and their units with the corresponding constant-coefficient ones. The same strict augmentation $Q_m(B)\to S_m$ after tensor with a K-flat $B$-representative has an isomorphism on derived limits because its restriction does, and exact restriction detects isomorphisms by cohomology of the underlying sheaves. This proves the completed-coefficient assertion and compatibility of both completion isomorphisms under restriction.
